title: Japanese Knot Bag
summary: A small reversible-look wristlet: the long handle slips through the short one to close it.
description: The knot bag (sometimes called an azuma-style or knot wristlet) is a traditional Japanese shape: one long and one short handle. Thread the long handle through the short loop to close the bag, or carry it over your wrist. It's fully lined with every seam hidden, and it's a lovely introduction to sewing curves.

materials.name: Outer fabric
materials.why: Outside of the bag and handles.
alternatives: A furoshiki or vintage kimono cotton

materials.name: Lining fabric
materials.why: Inside — it shows on the handle edges, so choose a contrast you like.

pieces.name: Outer body
markings: Notch both outer side edges 32 cm below the long-handle top — side seams stop here

pieces.name: Lining body
markings: Notch both outer side edges 32 cm below the long-handle top
Mark a 10 cm turning gap in the bottom of ONE piece

steps.title: Press your fabrics
steps.text: Pre-wash and press both fabrics. Cotton and linen with a little body make the handles hold their shape.

steps.title: Print the pattern piece
steps.text: This bag has curves, so print the pattern piece at 100% scale (Print pattern), check the test square, and tape the pages together. One pattern piece is used four times.
steps.beginner: Printing means the curves come out exactly as designed. The short and long handles must not be swapped — the label on the print shows which is which.
steps.alt: The knot bag pattern piece: a rounded body with a short handle on the left and a long handle on the right, 34 cm wide.

steps.title: Cut the outer
steps.text: Fold the outer fabric right sides together and pin the pattern through both layers. Cutting through two layers gives you a mirrored pair — exactly what you need. Transfer the side notches.
warnings: Cut slowly round the curves with the tips of sharp scissors, keeping your other hand clear of the blades.

steps.title: Cut the lining
steps.text: Cut a mirrored pair from the lining fabric the same way and transfer the notches.

steps.title: Sew the outer sides and bottom
steps.text: Place the outer pieces right sides together. Sew from one notch, down the side, across the bottom and up to the other notch with a 1 cm seam. Backstitch at both notches. Clip into the seam allowance at the rounded corners.
steps.alt: Two outer pieces right sides together, stitched down both sides and across the bottom, stopping at the side notches.

steps.title: Sew the lining the same way
steps.text: Repeat with the lining, but leave a 10 cm gap in the middle of the bottom seam for turning.
steps.alt: The lining pieces stitched the same way with a 10 cm gap left in the bottom seam.

steps.title: Nest outer inside lining
steps.text: Turn the outer bag right side out. Push it inside the lining (lining still wrong side out) so the right sides face each other. Match the side seams and line up every handle and curve. Pin all along the top edges.

args.label: outer inside lining — right sides together

steps.title: Sew round the curves and handles
steps.text: Sew with a 1 cm seam along the inner scoop between the handles and along both long edges of every handle, stopping 3 cm before each handle end. Leave the four handle ends open — they are joined later. Backstitch at every stop.
steps.expert: Sew inner curve + both handle edges RST at 1 cm; stop 3 cm short of handle ends.
steps.beginner: Think of it as sewing round the whole top edge of a bag, except the four little handle ends, which stay open so the handles can be joined later. Go slowly around the curve, stopping with the needle down to pivot slightly as you go.
steps.alt: Stitching following the inner curve between the handles and both edges of each handle, with the handle ends left open.

steps.title: Clip the curves
steps.text: Clip into the seam allowance every 1.5 cm around the inner curve, close to but not through the stitching, so it lies smooth when turned.

steps.title: Turn right side out
steps.text: Pull the whole bag through the gap in the lining. Push the handles out fully with a point turner or chopstick and push the lining down inside the bag. Press the curved edges so the seam sits right on the edge.

steps.title: Join the handle ends
steps.text: Take the two SHORT handle ends. Pull the lining layers out of the way and pin the two outer ends right sides together; sew across with 1 cm. Do the same for the two lining ends. Press open. Repeat with the two LONG handle ends. Tuck the remaining short gaps on each handle edge in line with the seams.

els.text: short to short · long to long

steps.beginner: It's fiddly: the handle becomes a loop and the fabric twists a little. Keep the outer and lining layers separate while you sew each ring, and check nothing is twisted before sewing.
steps.alt: Outer handle ends sewn right sides together beside lining handle ends sewn right sides together.

steps.title: Close the openings
steps.text: Slip-stitch (ladder-stitch) the short open sections on each handle edge, then close the lining gap by machine or by hand.

steps.title: Topstitch all edges
steps.text: Topstitch 5 mm from every edge — round the inner curve and both edges of each handle — to keep the lining from rolling out.

steps.title: Tie the knot
steps.text: Slip the long handle through the short loop and carry it on your wrist. To open, slide the long handle back out.

visual.label: Long handle through the short loop

review.note: Sample pattern; dimensions are internally consistent but not yet test-sewn.
